hints: Look closely at the first generation result. 100% medium DNA after one round in $^{14}N$ tells you exactly what each DNA molecule must contain.
Remember semi-conservative replication. Each old strand stays whole and acts as a template, and all new strands in $^{14}N$ medium can only contain $^{14}N$.
walkthrough:
**Start with the parental and first generation**

Think like a detective. Parental DNA is 100% heavy, so both strands are $^{15}N$.

After one round in $^{14}N$, all DNA is 100% medium. That only makes sense if each molecule has one old $^{15}N$ strand and one new $^{14}N$ strand.

**Apply semi-conservative replication to round two**

In semi-conservative replication, the two strands unzip and stay whole. Each becomes a template for a new strand.

Because the bacteria are still in $^{14}N$, every newly made strand must be only $^{14}N$.

**Predict the second generation molecules**

Take the two first-generation molecules (each $^{15}N$ + $^{14}N$) and replicate them:
$$2 \text{ medium molecules} \rightarrow 2 \text{ medium } (^{15}N + ^{14}N) + 2 \text{ light } (^{14}N + ^{14}N)$$
That is 50% medium and 50% light, exactly matching the diagram. This is row A.

options.A: Correct. Medium molecules keep one original $^{15}N$ strand plus one new $^{14}N$ strand, while light molecules have two $^{14}N$ strands. This gives 50% medium and 50% light.
options.B: Incorrect. A molecule with two $^{15}N$ strands would be heavy, not medium, and heavy DNA is not seen after growth in $^{14}N$.
options.C: Incorrect. Two $^{15}N$ strands would be heavy, not medium, and a $^{14}N$ plus $^{15}N$ molecule would be medium, not light.
options.D: Incorrect. Strands stay whole and are not mixed half and half. Replication is semi-conservative, so each strand is either all $^{15}N$ (old) or all $^{14}N$ (new).
